item.title: GRAINS CLIMB FRIDAY, CATTLE STALL BEFORE COF WEEK
item.description: Corn closed Friday at $5.29, up 1.7% on the week's last session, and wheat gained 1.8% to $7.04 on nothing more than a bearish China trade story running out of sellers. Cattle held flat at $218.85 with a Cattle on Feed report still ahead. Action: Nothing to do at $5.29 corn; a close back below $5.20 confirms Friday's bounce was just short-covering. • Grains Bounce On Empty News • Cattle Flat, Feeders Firm Ahead Of COF Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-26

item.title: GRAINS SIT STILL, CATTLE SLIP AGAIN BEFORE COF

item.title: CRUDE RUNS TO $93 AS HORMUZ TRAFFIC STAYS THIN
item.description: Crude added 2.1% to $93.19 and it isn't demand talking, it's one vessel crossing the Strait of Hormuz Wednesday, stuck below the 10-day average with the Iran-Hormuz cycle still refusing to fully unwind. Action: Lock diesel needs now; a close above $6.55 on the rack price is the next reason to pre-buy fall fuel, not wait. • Crude Runs On Thin Hormuz Traffic • Grains Give Back More Ground • Cattle Grind Higher Again Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-24

item.title: GRAINS GIVE BACK THE CHINA POP AHEAD OF XI SUMMIT
item.description: Corn settled $5.29, down 3½ cents, wheat down a penny and three-quarters, both giving back Monday's China-hope pop before Thursday's Trump-Xi summit even opens. Cattle fell 0.8% to $219.35 the day after a 2.4% jump on record-low placements, that's real profit-taking, not a reversal of the placements story. Action: Corn: no action above $5.29, but a settle below $5.27 says the China pop is fully unwound, price the next 10%. • Grains Fade The Summit Pop • Cattle Cool After Placement Pop Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-23

item.title: CORN RALLIES ON CHINA HOPES; CATTLE JUMP 2.4%
item.description: Corn ran 15 cents to three-week highs and beans gained 24 cents overnight on fresh hope for a US-China trade deal, but both gave it back into the close, corn settling $5.38 and beans $13.19, both down on the day. Cattle didn't fade: $221.15, up 2.4% on record low placements. Action: Live cattle at $221.15: nothing to sell into a 2.4% up day off record low placements, hold for $222 confirmation. • Grains Fade The China Pop • Cattle Ignore The Grain Fade • Crude Reverses On Iran Hope Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-22

item.title: BEANS FLAT, DIESEL AT $6.50, CRUDE BREAKS ON IRAN THAW
item.description: Soybeans sit at $13.10, off a penny and a half, still waiting on Xi. item.title: BEANS SANK FRIDAY; SUMMIT WEEK OPENS WITH CROSSED SIGNALS
item.description: Soybeans closed Friday at $13.03, down 16 cents on the week's last session as funds took profits ahead of the Trump-Xi summit set for Sep 24. Crude broke 5.6% the same day, its biggest single-session drop in weeks, while diesel stayed near record highs regardless. Action: Nothing to do at $13.03 beans over the weekend; a Monday close below $12.90 says the summit trade is unwinding, not building. • BEANS PRICE THE SUMMIT, NOT THE CROP • DIESEL STAYS TIGHT AS CRUDE BREAKS • CATTLE FIRM, FEEDER SUPPLY THE STORY Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-20

item.title: CRUDE RETREATS; TRUMP-XI SUMMIT HANGS OVER BEANS
item.description: Soybeans closed Friday at $13.03, down 7½ cents, and the fund liquidation was straightforward: nobody wanted to hold a long position into a weekend with the Trump-Xi summit on September 24 still unresolved. Wheat led the grain complex lower at $7.13, off 11½ cents. item.title: CRUDE BREAKS 5.6%; BEANS WAIT FOR XI
item.description: Saudi Aramco's Gulf reroute -- started this week after the East-West pipeline shifted 60 million barrels back through the Persian Gulf -- knocked crude down 5.6% to **$95.47**, its biggest single-session drop in months. Relief, not shortage, is what the market priced Friday. Diesel harvest risk hasn't left; it just got cheaper to ignore. Action: Unpriced new-crop beans: hold through the weekend. A Monday settle above $13.10 is the first reason to price anything before the Xi summit. • CRUDE BREAKS; ENERGY LEADS LOWER • BEANS WAIT FOR XI • CATTLE HOLD; FEEDERS SLIP Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-18

item.title: FARM BILL MOVES; EXPORT SALES PRINT AT 7:30
item.description: The Senate Ag Committee broke its August deadlock Wednesday, advancing Farm Bill 2.0 on a 12-11 vote -- the first real legislative movement since the Aug 6 party-line failure. Beans settled at $13.26, off 3.5 cents, leaving the Nov contract a dime short of the level that would have triggered new-crop pricing for most operations. Action: New-crop beans: if Export Sales top 600K MT and Nov '26 closes above $13.42, price the first 10%. • EXPORT SALES IN FOCUS • CRUDE EASES; DIESEL STORY DEEPENS Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-17

item.title: SEPTEMBER WASDE PRINTS; BEANS GIVE BACK 24 CENTS
item.description: The September WASDE printed Thursday, and Friday the market said what it thought: soybeans at $12.99 gave back 24 cents, the sharpest single-session drop in weeks, while December corn at $5.32 actually added a nickel. The USDA printed something, the funds sold beans and held corn, and now the question is whether $12.99 is the new floor or the first step lower. Friday's WASDE report sent soybeans lower and corn sideways, while crude fell hard on the Saudi pipeline story reversing course. • WASDE PRINTS; BEANS FOLD → If you have unpriced new-crop beans, $12.99 is the line. A close below $12.85 next week says the WASDE break has legs; price on that signal, not ahead of it. • CRUDE FALLS ON SAUDI PIPELINE REVERSAL • CATTLE FIRMS; HOGS SLIP Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-12

item.title: WASDE AT 11 CT; CRUDE DROPS 4%, BEANS FIRM
item.description: Soybeans firmed to $13.17 at the 52-week high while crude fell hard to $99.06, its sharpest one-session drop in weeks, as the whole complex repositioned ahead of the September WASDE at 11 CT. The meal/bean side held; the energy side gave back two weeks of war premium in one morning. WASDE decides which part of the market read this week correctly. September WASDE prints in hours while crude's biggest single-day drop in weeks reshapes the input-cost math for fall fieldwork. • WASDE POSITIONING; BEANS AT 52-WEEK HIGH → If you have unpriced new-crop beans above $13.17, hold through 11 CT and let the WASDE print before making a sale. • CRUDE DROPS HARD; DIESEL HITS $6 → Today's crude pullback to $99 is the window to price fall diesel, not a reason to wait for $95. • CATTLE FIRMS; FEEDLOT MARGINS STILL DEEP RED Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-11

item.title: BRENT HITS $100; GRAINS AND CATTLE FOLLOW
item.description: WTI settled at **$95.26**, its highest close in two months, after the US destroyed five Iranian tankers and Iran struck US forces in Jordan, the sharpest re-escalation of the Iran-Hormuz cycle since its July flare. Wheat added 11 cents on war-premium buying; harvest diesel has no global slack. The September WASDE lands Friday into a market that just re-priced risk. The next 48 hours are not quiet. US strikes on Iranian tankers push crude to a two-month high, dragging harvest input costs higher and lifting grains on war-premium buying. • ENERGY LEADS THE COMPLEX → If fall diesel needs are unpriced, today's Brent close above $100 says this is the window, not a reason to wait for a pullback. • WHEAT LIFTS ON WAR BID • CATTLE AND HOGS RUN HIGHER Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-09

item.title: WHEAT BREAKS 3.4%; SEPTEMBER WASDE COUNTDOWN BEGINS
item.description: Wheat closed $7.16, down 3.4% Friday, the biggest single-session drop in the complex. Corn drifted to $5.12 on light volume as Labor Day weekend stripped the room. Beans held better at $12.94, off just 1.1%. The whole week telegraphs one thing: the funds took profits before the holiday and are waiting for Thursday's export sales and Friday's WASDE to decide their next move. Friday's pre-holiday profit-taking hit wheat hardest while corn and beans drifted; the September 11 WASDE is the week's make-or-break event. • WHEAT BREAKS; GRAINS DRIFT • CATTLE QUIET; TRUMP ORDERS MOVE • ENERGY AND INPUTS INTO HARVEST → If you have unpriced fall diesel needs, the EIA crack-spread data says the current rack price is not the top of the range. item.title: WHEAT DROPS 3.4%; DIESEL TIGHTENS INTO HARVEST
item.description: Wheat closed Friday at $7.16, down 3.4%, the sharpest single-session drop in this complex in weeks. Diesel crack spreads widened to record levels according to EIA data, meaning the fuel bill for first-pass harvest is higher than any budget penciled in last spring. The September 11 WASDE is six days out and the market is walking in with a bearish lean on wheat and a diesel problem. Friday's close put wheat at its worst session in weeks while diesel crack spreads widened, squeezing fall fieldwork budgets before the September 11 WASDE. • WHEAT BREAKS; GRAINS DRIFT • CATTLE QUIET; POLICY NOISE RISES • DIESEL TIGHTENS; CRUDE HOLDS → If you haven't locked fall diesel at current rack prices, the EIA data says waiting is not working in your favor. item.title: CATTLE BREAK ON BEEF IMPORTS; BEANS FIRM
item.description: Cattle at $212.40 and feeders at $320.80 are barely off, but the news under them is worse than the ticks: Trump is opening lean beef imports AND Mexico resumes feeder shipments, two supply hits the same morning. Beans at $12.94 are up 1.5% on a different story -- soybean oil ran 3% as diesel crack spreads hit records, pulled higher by the U.S.-Iran exchange of strikes overnight (ongoing since late August) that cut Hormuz tanker traffic to four crossings Tuesday from a 13-vessel average. Two markets, two completely different problems. Trump's lean beef import expansion and Mexico feeder resumption hit cattle markets just as soybeans push 1.5% higher on oil-crush demand. • CATTLE: SUPPLY SHOCK LANDS → If you have cattle to price, the import headline is not priced in at $212.40. Lock something before Thursday's export sales confirm or deny the demand side. • BEANS AND OIL FIRM HARD • WHEAT DROPS; OATS RUN Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-02

item.title: WHEAT FIRMS; EPA BIOFUEL EXEMPTIONS HIT THE BOARD
item.description: Wheat is the only grain doing anything today, up nearly 15 cents to $7.60 while corn barely twitched and beans gave back three cents. The real story isn't the price action: it's the EPA quietly handing 18 refineries full RFS exemptions this morning, removing 1.76 billion gallons of biofuel obligation from the 2025 compliance year. Corn's ethanol demand argument just got smaller. Chicago wheat rose 1.9% on overnight momentum while EPA granted 1.76 billion gallons of RFS exemptions, a direct hit to ethanol demand math. • WHEAT LEADS; CORN IGNORES EPA → December corn at $5.37 with harvest beginning: the EPA exemption is a demand headwind the board hasn't moved on yet. If you have unpriced new-crop, the September WASDE on the 10th is your next real window, but don't assume the price holds there. • HOGS FIRM; CATTLE HOLD • CRUDE UP; NATGAS SLIPS Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-01

item.title: WHEAT LEADS THE WEEK; CORN PRICED FOR HARVEST
item.description: Wheat ended the week at $7.67, up 22 cents Friday on heat-driven supply stress, the biggest one-day move in the complex. Beans tagged along at $12.76, near a 52-week high. The story this week: the August WASDE cut yields, the Pro Farmer tour confirmed stress, and December corn at $5.37 is pricing a tighter crop. The question now is whether September has a reason to add to that premium. Chicago wheat closed up 22 cents Friday, beans followed, and December corn held $5.37 as combines roll toward the Belt. • GRAINS: WHEAT LEADS, BEANS HOLD → December corn at $5.365: if Friday's window did not move you, this is the same price. item.title: WHEAT RUNS, BEANS HOLD; HEATWAVE BIDS THE COMPLEX
item.description: Chicago wheat rose sharply to $7.66, up 21 cents on the session, and meal ran to $338.70, up 2.9%, as a heatwave forecast into Labor Day weekend gave late-summer grain bulls something to work with. Beans joined them, adding $12.78 nearby on a 1.3% gain. Corn sat out the party, easing a penny and a half to $5.11. When three of four grains move on weather and one doesn't, that's the market telling you corn's story is already priced. A forecasted heatwave into Labor Day lit up wheat and meal Friday while corn eased and gold sold off hard. • WHEAT AND MEAL LEAD HIGHER • BEANS HOLD; CORN SITS OUT → December corn at $5.36: if you have unpriced new-crop bushels, this is the window. Combines are coming. • CATTLE MARK TIME; SCREWWORM CLOCK TICKS Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-08-28
